name: Marble Queen Pothos
description: One of the most striking pothos varieties, Marble Queen is a heavily variegated cultivar of Epipremnum aureum whose heart-shaped leaves are splashed and streaked with creamy-white and green in a marbled pattern so dense that some leaves are nearly half white. As easy and forgiving as classic Golden Pothos, it trails elegantly from shelves and hanging baskets or climbs a moss pole with aerial roots. The one key difference is light: because so much of each leaf lacks chlorophyll, Marble Queen needs brighter indirect light than the all-green types to keep its variegation crisp and to grow at a reasonable pace - in low light it grows slowly and the new leaves lose their marbling and revert toward solid green. Give it good light and consistent-but-not-soggy watering and it rewards you with cascading, painterly foliage that looks far fussier than it actually is.
toxicity: Toxic to cats, dogs and horses. Chewing it causes mouth pain and swelling, drooling, vomiting and difficulty swallowing.

symptoms: Pain and swelling of the mouth, tongue and lips

careInstructions: Water when top 1-2 inches of soil are dry - typically weekly
Provide medium to bright indirect light to keep variegation strong - brighter than Golden Pothos needs
Avoid harsh direct sun, which scorches the white sections
Prune regularly to maintain length and encourage fuller, bushier growth
Propagates easily in water - cut just below a node
Wipe leaves monthly to remove dust and enhance variegation
Fertilize every other month during spring and summer with diluted balanced fertilizer - skip winter
Grows slower than all-green pothos - normal for a heavily variegated plant
commonProblems: Loss of variegation / reverting to green: Insufficient light - move to a brighter spot
Brown, crispy patches on white areas: Sunburn from direct light or low humidity
Yellow leaves: Usually overwatering - allow soil to dry more between waterings
Brown leaf tips: Fluoride or chlorine sensitivity - use filtered water
Leggy growth with sparse leaves: Not enough light
Root rot: Overwatering or poor drainage - ensure the pot has drainage holes

fertilizing.tip: Fertilize every other month during spring and summer with diluted balanced fertilizer - skip winter

whatsNormal: Variegated pothos grow more slowly than all-green ones and need brighter light to keep their color — in low light the pale patches shrink.
Older leaves yellow and drop over time, so leaves bunch toward the ends of the vines — prune stems back to keep it full.

propagation.tip: Cut below a node and root it in water or moist mix.

flags.note: Sources cover Epipremnum aureum, not the 'Marble Queen' cultivar. The brighter light for variegation follows NC State and Clemson's notes on variegated pothos.
Winter watering interval (10 days) is our estimate — the sources only say to reduce watering from fall to late winter.
Fertilizing monthly → every other month, matching the Pothos research (NC State, Wisconsin).
